title: FP-DeErr: Application-Oriented Error Decomposition for Foundation Potentials
abstract: Foundation potentials (FPs) have emerged as a new basis for atomistic modeling. While their evaluation using average energy and force errors often indicates near-DFT accuracy, their performance in practical computational studies remains inconsistent. While recent benchmarks evaluate FPs on downstream computational tasks, the underlying errors that determine task success or failure are not always clear. Here, we develop FP-DeErr, an application-oriented error-decomposition framework that resolves FP errors according to the physically meaningful quantities, configurations, and computational stages governing specific tasks. Rather than averaging errors over an entire dataset, FP-DeErr uses decomposed error metrics devised for physically meaningful quantities, focusing on the configurations where errors arise and matter most. We demonstrate FP-DeErr by evaluating multiple state-of-the-art FPs on three fundamental tasks: force prediction for atomistic simulations, energy ranking for substitutional and vacancy orderings, and ion/vacancy migration. These error-decomposition metrics resolve force errors among highly accurate, large-error, and far-from-equilibrium atoms; relative-energy errors among competing orderings, phases, and compositions; and ion migration errors among endpoints and along-path errors. By identifying where FP errors arise, this error decomposition provides targeted guidance for FP development. FP-DeErr also provides an open benchmark, evaluation code, and a public leaderboard for rigorous FP assessment.

title: RenderFormer-V2: Neural Rendering with Heterogeneous Scene Primitives
abstract: We present 'RenderFormer-V2', a unified learned transformer-based neural rendering model, complementary to modern physics-based rendering systems, that can handle diverse light-transport effects such as caustics, volumetric scattering, environment lighting, textured and displaced surfaces and out-of-distribution materials without per-scene training or specialized code. RenderFormer-V2 models global light transport as a sequence-to-sequence transformation. Following its predecessor, RenderFormer-V2 also employs a two stage process: a view-independent stage that resolves intra-scene primitive to primitive transport, and a view-dependent stage that transforms the internal neural scene representation into image pixels. Different from RenderFormer, our model employs a novel combined windowed-attention and rendering-informed attention sink in the view-independent stage to improve scalability while maintaining render accuracy. To further improve versatility, RenderFormerV2 supports heterogeneous scene primitives, including environment maps and participating media, and it employs a material encoding independent of the underlying surface reflectance model that encodes material appearance via a novel neural embedding. We demonstrate the versatility of RenderFormer-V2 on a variety of scenes and perform an extensive ablation of the improved attention mechanism.

title: From global optimization to transition state search: an automated workflow for surface reaction barriers
abstract: Reaction barrier calculations present the major bottleneck in the systematic exploration of surface reaction networks in heterogeneous catalysis via atomistic simulations. Each transition-state search introduces a high-dimensional configuration space of initial and final-state combinations that must be explored to identify the minimum-energy pathway with the lowest activation barrier. Typically, this task is delegated to human chemical intuition as user input to, e.g., nudged elastic band (NEB) calculations, since its automation remains challenging. Here, we introduce NEBscape, a fully automated workflow for transition-state searches that requires no human intervention. Initial and final states are generated via global optimization and systematically combined through atom mapping, symmetry alignment, and heuristic selection to yield a tractable set of NEB calculations. We benchmark NEBscape against diverse reactions and model surfaces from the OC20NEB database, where it identifies, on average, lower transition-state energies and produces minimum-energy pathways with high chemical fidelity to the target reactions.

title: Low–Energy Metastable Ensemble–Involving Ostwald Ripening of Au Nanoclusters on Anatase TiO2(101) under Oxidizing Conditions
abstract: Supported Au nanoclusters are highly effective catalysts but are susceptible to deactivation via sintering. While Ostwald ripening (OR) is a primary sintering mechanism, its atomic-scale pathways on the anatase TiO2 surface remain poorly understood. Using neural network potential, we investigate the OR process of Au nanoclusters supported on TiO2(101) under oxidizing conditions, identifying Au and AuO as the primary mobile species. A systematic monomer detachment mapping (MDMAP) workflow is developed to efficiently sample the detachment landscape.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Bridging simulation length scales with cellular automata
abstract: Multiscale simulation requires coupling physics models that operate at different characteristic length and time scales, because no single method spans the range needed for most problems of interest. Moving to a coarser-grained representation unlocks longer length and time scales, but it discards the microscopic interactions that build morphology. A fine-grained model can be initialized from an arbitrary packing and left to self-assemble into a physically meaningful structure; a lower-resolution model cannot, and must inherit its starting configuration from a higher-fidelity simulation. The length scales accessible to the coarse-grained model are therefore set not by the coarse-grained method itself, but by the largest fine-grained configuration that can be affordably equilibrated. A representative example is the scale-up from particle-based molecular dynamics (MD) to a lattice-based representation such as kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC). In this work, we present a cellular automata (CA) approach for generating arbitrarily large lattice starting configurations. CA is a natural fit for this task: short-ranged local rules drive the evolution of a lattice, and their repeated application gives rise to emergent long-range order, thematically mirroring how short-ranged interactions in MD produce self-assembled morphology. We use a configuration from a higher-fidelity simulation as a training set and learn the CA rules from it via logistic regression. As a proof of principle, we develop these rules for a hydrated anion exchange membrane (AEM), generate new starting configurations, and benchmark their performance in mesoscale kMC simulations against an MD-derived "ground truth." We then demonstrate the ability to generate substantially larger lattices and show that their behavior in kMC is consistent with that of the smaller CA benchmark configurations.

title: GraphNOSE: A Graph Transformer in Olfaction
abstract: Predicting olfactory qualities from molecular structure is an open problem in chemoinformatics. Although linear models can link molecular features to odor descriptors, they often fail when extrapolating to novel chemical scaffolds, extreme molecular weights, or complex odor mixtures. To address this, we introduce GraphNOSE, an open-source graph transformer framework that predicts multi-label odor descriptors from simplified molecular-input line-entry system (SMILES) strings for single molecules and binary mixtures. By integrating positional and structural encodings within a transformer-based graph architecture, GraphNOSE achieves strong performance with six times fewer parameters than standard graph neural network (GNN) baseline while consistently outperforming linear models, molecular language model embeddings, molecular fingerprints, and baseline GNNs by an average area under the ROC curve (AUROC) margin of 4.52% (p < 0.01). GraphNOSE achieves an AUROC of 84% on out-of-distribution compounds (OODs). This exceeds the current state-of-the-art GNN for OOD in olfaction (Open-POM: 81%, p < 0.001), and identifies conditions under which linear models empirically fail. Finally, we apply XAI (explainable AI) methods to identify which substructures and molecular features drive odor predictions, yielding insights consistent with chemical intuition and grounded in the model's learned representations. Together, these results establish GraphNOSE as a scalable and interpretable architecture for olfactory prediction that generalizes to structurally distinct compounds underrepresented in current perceptual databases.

title: Differentiable Solvation Shell Model for Rational Electrolyte Design
abstract: Tailoring Li+ solvation structures has emerged as a promising design principle across multiple Li metal battery (LMB) electrolytes, with localized high concentration electrolytes (LHCE) emerging as a leading candidate. However, rational design of these electrolytes remains limited by a poor quantitative understanding of how molecular properties govern Li+ solvation shell composition. Here we introduce a mean field modeling framework, built on an Ising model, that predicts solvation shell composition from donor number (DN), acceptor number (AN), molar ratio, and molecular size. This framework is end-to-end differentiable, which enables parameterization directly from molecular dynamics (MD) solvation structures via gradient-based optimization. Focusing on LHCE, the model achieves 10.7% RMSE and R2=0.87 for shell composition, 2.3% RMSE on free solvent ratio, and further reproduces solvation trends in real LHCE electrolytes, at a fraction of MD's cost. Our model also shows good generalizability on other electrolyte systems in addition to LHCE. Analysis of its interaction terms shows that DN dominates Li+ solvation energetics, providing a thermodynamic basis for empirical DN-based design rules. We further demonstrate the model's design utility on the LiTFSI/tetraglyme (G4) system absent from training. The model identifies fluorobenzene (FB) as a promising diluent and predicts a salt-concentration window with anion-rich solvation shells and low free solvent, favorable for stable anion-derived SEIs and high oxidative stability, respectively. This prediction is validated by higher-fidelity MD. This work establishes an interpretable differentiable framework for predicting Li+ solvation shell composition, with potential to extend to other electrolyte classes.

title: The convergent laboratory: when AI reasoning, autonomous experiments, high performance and quantum computing reshape chemistry
abstract: This Comment emerges from TPC26 (https://tpc26.org), a conference convening leaders from academia, national laboratories, and industry who are reshaping materials science discovery. The meeting explored how AI, autonomous agents, self-driving labs, higher performance and quantum computing converge to amplify their individual impact on materials science discovery. The perspectives here reflect the firsthand experiences of researchers at these frontiers and capture the essence of this global endeavor. As AI-driven reasoning, autonomous agentic frameworks, self-driving laboratories, and fault-tolerant quantum processors mature simultaneously, we offer this Comment as a reference at what we believe is a tipping point of transformative advances and productive disruption in the chemical sciences.

title: Attention-Driven Framework for Non-Rigid Medical Image Registration
abstract: Deformable medical image registration is a fundamental task in medical image analysis, with applications in disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and image-guided interventions. Despite recent advances in deep learning based registration, accurate alignment under large anatomical deformations remains challenging, particularly when deformation plausibility must be preserved. In this paper, we propose an Attention-Driven Framework for Non-Rigid Medical Image Registration (AD-RegNet).
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

title: Intramolecular oxygen coupling mediates water oxidation on an oxide electrocatalyst
abstract: Understanding the mechanistic pathways of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential for guiding the design of catalytic materials and advancing sustainable energy technologies, as sluggish OER kinetics remain a major limitation. Here, using 18 O isotope labeling experiments, we provide kinetic evidence for oxygen coupling occurring within the lattice of a Bi 0.2 Sr 0.8 CoO 3-δ perovskite catalyst, unveiling an OER pathway distinct from conventional mechanisms and closely analogous to that of Photosystem II.

title: Silylium-Ion-Promoted Cycloisomerization of Silicon-Tethered Enynes
abstract: A series of four silylium-ion-promoted enyne cycloisomerization reactions is reported. Various silicon-tethered 1,5-, 1,6-, and 1,7-enynes engage in chemoselective π-activation of either unsaturated branch by the formation of β,β- or β,β’-bis(silicon)-stabilized vinyl cations (from the alkyne branch) or a β-silicon-stabilized carbenium ion (from the alkene branch). Subsequent ring closures lead to a six-membered ring (silinane) in three cases, while one 1,5-enyne cyclizes to give a five-membered ring (silole). The silole system stands out as the exocyclic silyl group is lost by protolysis, followed by proton-mediated, thermodynamically controlled migration of an aryl substituent. The reaction mechanisms can be rationalized by silicon-controlled carbocation formation with termination by either allylation of a carbenium-ion intermediate with an allylsilane or a Friedel–Crafts reaction with an arene. The proton from the Wheland intermediate is captured by proton-into-silylium ion interconversion, again employing an allylsilane reagent.

title: Quantitative Prediction of Coal-Gangue Content Using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy and Physics-Informed Machine Learning
abstract: Quantitative determination of gangue content is important for efficient coal use and intelligent coal-gangue separation. We combine transmission terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS), multidomain feature fusion, and machine learning to predict gangue mass fraction in coal-gangue mixtures. Time- and frequency-domain signals, refractive index, absorption and extinction coefficients, and complex permittivity were extracted from samples with different gangue contents. Five-fold cross-validation was used to compare random forest, support vector regression, Gaussian process regression, an artificial neural network, and an Effective Medium Theory-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (EMT-PINN). EMT-PINN achieved the best performance, with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.81 ± 0.15, a mean absolute error (MAE) 3.17 ± 0.59%, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 5.79 ± 0.21%, compared with R2 values of 0.72 ± 0.08, 0.61 ± 0.21, 0.74 ± 0.11, and 0.64 ± 0.18 for RF, SVR, GPR, and ANN, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of physics-informed THz spectroscopy for rapid and physically interpretable quantitative characterization of coal-gangue mixtures.

title: Diffusion TV: Experiencing Diffusion Models through Tangible, Embodied Interaction
abstract: Diffusion TV is an interactive AI art installation that offers a tangible and embodied experience of diffusion models through a modified CRT TV. By physically manipulating the TV's antenna, audiences control the clarity of AI-generated images and sounds, metaphorically enacting the denoising process that underlies diffusion-based generation. Using the tuning knob, participants switch between three channels featuring AI-generated animals from the Past (extinct species), Present (endangered species), and Future (speculative creatures), situating the interaction within a temporal and ecological narrative. Through continuous audiovisual feedback and physical interaction, Diffusion TV foregrounds the generative process over final outputs, allowing audiences to explore intermediate states as experiential material. Rather than providing explicit technical explanation, the work presents an alternative, embodied mode of explainable AI that invites exploratory engagement with and reflection on generative technologies.

title: Directing Cluster Nuclearity in Semiconducting Lead Thioborates Built from Adamantane and Superadamantane Boron–Sulfur Clusters
abstract: Metal thioborates remain an underdeveloped class of chalcogenides because their synthesis is highly sensitive to vessel reactivity, amorphization, and the transport of volatile boron–sulfur species, all of which frustrate phase-selective access to well-defined cluster-based solids. Here we report controlled access to two tetragonal, noncentrosymmetric chiral lead thioborates, Pb2B2S5 (P41212) and Pb2B4S8 (I41), enabled by tuning stoichiometry, tube geometry, headspace, and cooling protocols to limit volatile transport and promote phase selectivity.

title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence
abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges, we developed Squidly, a sequence-only tool that leverages contrastive representation learning with a biology-informed, rationally designed pairing scheme to distinguish catalytic from non-catalytic residues using per-token Protein Language Model embeddings. Squidly surpasses state-of-the-art ML annotation methods in catalytic residue prediction while remaining sufficiently fast to enable wide-scale screening of databases. We ensemble Squidly with BLAST to provide an efficient tool that annotates catalytic residues with high precision and recall for both in- and out-of-distribution sequences.

title: Quantitative Delineation of the Morphological Heterogeneity of Anisotropic Nanostructures via Machine-Learning-Augmented Electron Microscopy.
abstract: Precise synthesis and engineering of homogeneous anisotropic nanostructures are essential to realize their shape-dependent physicochemical properties for different applications. However, due to the difficulty in controlling factors influencing nucleation and growth, many reported anisotropic nanostructures exhibit substantial heterogeneity, particularly in their size and shape distributions. Current methods for assessing nanostructure heterogeneity, whether ensemble- or single-particle-based techniques, are limited in the types of readout information, resolution, and throughput.

title: Breaking the autophagy-oxidative stress vicious cycle in Alzheimer's disease: Lactiflorin unlocks P62 dual phosphorylation via ULK1 targeting
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceThe dried root of Paeonia lactiflora Pall. has a long history of medicinal use in traditional Chinese medicine. Classical materia medica and traditional practice describe Paeonia-related medicinal materials for headache, dizziness, restlessness, and other neurological or behavioral manifestations, particularly in disorders traditionally associated with blood or yin deficiency and liver-yang hyperactivity. Modern pharmacological studies have further demonstrated neuroprotective and antioxidant effects of Paeonia lactiflora and its bioactive monoterpene glycosides.

title: Direct measurement of PET hydrolase interfacial kinetics reveals catalysis-independent surface remodelling
abstract: How PET hydrolases engage solid plastic has been inferred almost entirely from soluble analogs and surfactant-stabilised nanoparticle suspensions, and reported affinities span orders of magnitude. Here we measure it directly, depositing thin amorphous PET films onto gold surface plasmon resonance chips and following enzyme binding to authentic polymer in real time. Four PET hydrolases, LCC, LCC-ICCG, IsPETase-EHA and TfCut2, all bind with nanomolar apparent affinity and surface residence half-lives of tens of minutes.

title: Thermophoresis effects on Sn-W/ C₃H₈O₂ nanomaterial using intelligent neuro-computing paradigm: Yamada-Ota model
abstract: The Yamada-Ota thermal conductivity model, along with an intelligent neuro-computing paradigm, is commonly used to study the thermophysical behavior of Sn-W/C₃H₈O₂ nanomaterials during thermophoresis and Soret-Dufour effects. The concept has numerous applications, including electronic device cooling, solar energy systems, thermal energy storage, chemical reactors, biomedical heat transfer, and nanofluid-based heat exchangers. It accurately predicts effective thermal conductivity, heat and mass transfer, and nanoparticle transport, while the intelligent predictive-computing approach improves prediction accuracy, lowers computational costs, and helps to optimize advanced thermal management systems and industrial processes. This report uses Intelligent Bayesian optimization trained by back propagating neural networks to examine the mass and heat transport parameters of a nanofluid made of Sn-W/C₃H₈O₂ nanoparticles dispersed in water. This study inspects the impacts of Soret and Dufour effects on Sn-W/C₃H₈O₂ hybrid nanomaterial under thermophoresis effects using Yamada-Ota model. The resulting higher-order nonlinear ODEs are numerically solved using MATLAB's bvp4c technique. The thermal field rises as increase the values of nanoparticles volume fraction.

title: Challenges in orbital current-driven domain wall motion in light metal/ferrimagnet heterostructures
abstract: Recent advances in spintronics suggest that orbital Hall currents generated by charge injection in light metals can provide nonequilibrium angular momentum without relying on strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we examine whether such orbital currents can drive domain wall (DW) motion in an amorphous ferrimagnetic alloy, Gd$_{25}$(Fe$_{9}$Co$_{1}$)$_{75}$ (GFC), where the rare-earth sublattice offers strong SOC for orbital-to-spin conversion. We compare three representative heterostructures: Pt/GFC as a spin Hall reference, light-metal (Mn or Ti)/GFC for direct orbital-current injection, and light-metal/Pt/GFC incorporating an ultrathin Pt layer for orbital-to-spin conversion. Whereas Pt/GFC exhibits robust and reproducible spin-orbit-torque-driven DW motion, no current-driven DW motion is detected in Mn/GFC or Ti/GFC. Second-harmonic Hall measurements nevertheless reveal finite damping-like torques in both Mn/GFC and Ti/GFC, demonstrating that angular-momentum transfer into GFC does occur but is far weaker than in Pt/GFC. Inserting a 1-nm-thick Pt conversion layer strongly enhances the damping-like torque and restores DW motion. Thickness-dependent analysis further shows that DW mobility and depinning thresholds correlate with the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and domain-wall width, highlighting weak torque conversion and insufficient interfacial stabilization of chiral DWs as key challenges for orbital-driven DW motion in light-metal/ferrimagnet heterostructures.

title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of (–)-TAN-67
abstract: (–)-TAN-67 is a synthetic opioid alkaloid that acts as a selective δ-opioid receptor (δ-OR) agonist and shares structural similarity to µ-opioid ligands, such as morphine, naltrexone, and many clinically employed derivatives. Previously, the synthesis of (–)-TAN-67 required preparing trans-fused (±)octahydroisoquinoline 1 followed by chiral resolution. The existing routes to access this key intermediate require 7–9 steps, produce 2–20% overall yield, produce racemic material, and have reproducibility issues.

title: Dramatic acceleration by silica gel under highly concentrated conditions: Aromatic halogenation and nitroaldol (Henry) reactions
abstract: Dramatic acceleration of aromatic halogenation and nitroaldol (Henry) reactions was achieved by the addition of silica gel under highly concentrated conditions. Bromination, chlorination, and iodination of various aromatic substrates were examined in the presence of silica gel under highly concentrated conditions, and significant acceleration was observed for many substrates compared with conventional conditions. The combination of silica gel and highly concentrated conditions also markedly accelerated nitroaldol (Henry) reactions of aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes.

title: Unveiling Surface Reaction Networks in Biomass-Derived Compound Upgrading
abstract: Biomass-derived platform molecules often undergo complex surface reactions in which productive routes compete with catalyst deactivation, limiting catalyst selectivity and stability. Identifying the molecular origins of these competing processes remains challenging, as conventional computational approaches generally rely on chemical intuition and hypothesis-driven rules, while strongly adsorbed intermediates and poisoning species remain difficult to characterize experimentally.

title: 1º Non-Anomeric Glycoboranes: Palladium Catalyzed Synthesis and Functionalization
abstract: The proliferation of methods for transforming the carbon–boron bond has made alkyl organoboranes prized intermediates in organic chemistry. Despite this versatility, the synthesis of borylated carbohydrates (i.e., “glycoboranes”) is largely limited to borylation at the anomeric position or chemistries that leverage glycals to introduce boron at C2 or C3. Herein, we describe a Pd-catalyzed, deiodinative borylation that installs a pinacol boronic ester moiety at the primary position of carbohydrates most distal to the anomeric center to afford 1º non-anomeric glycoboranes.

title: Probing Factors Important to Bulk Nanobubble Stability: A Molecular Dynamics Study
abstract: Bulk nanobubbles have attracted considerable attention because of their reported long-term stability. Yet this apparent stability appears inconsistent with classical predictions based on the Young–Laplace equation, and despite extensive theoretical and experimental studies, the underlying molecular mechanisms responsible remain unresolved. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations are used to evaluate the pressure–radius relationship for bulk nanobubbles and to investigate origins for possible deviations from classical Young–Laplace behaviour.

title: A DFT Study of Oxidative Lignin β-O-4 Bond Cleavage by Transition-Metal Catalysis
abstract: Biomass is the only viable source of renewable terrestrial carbon. Lignin, a rigid structure of biomass, has been investigated for its difficulty to depolymerize. β-O-4 linkages, which account for 50-60% of all inter-unit bonds, are the primary targets for breaking down the polymer to derive aromatic compounds. Although transition-metal-assisted oxidative cleavage has been identified as a promising method, the conventionally used 4d and 5d transition metals are scarce and expensive, limiting industrial scalability.

title: GPU-Accelerated Large-Scale Nonadiabatic Excited State Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics is essential for simulating photoinduced processes, but its application to large molecular systems is often limited by the cost of repeatedly evaluating excited-state energies, forces, and nonadiabatic couplings. Here, we present a GPU-accelerated implementation of trajectory surface hopping within PYSEQM (https://github.com/lanl/PYSEQM/), a PyTorch-based semiempirical quantum chemistry framework.

title: Vibrational energy pooling driven by collective light–matter coupling
abstract: Concentrating vibrational energy from multiple molecules onto selected members of an ensemble is central to mode-selective chemistry and molecular energy transport. Yet established mechanisms of vibrational energy pooling (VEP) rely on molecular collisions or strong intermolecular interactions. Here we demonstrate that collective vibrational strong coupling (VSC) provides a distinct route to VEP, with the optical cavity serving as an energetic intermediary.

title: Computational Elucidation of System-Dependent Excited-State Relaxation Mechanisms and Stokes Shifts in Indole-Based Chromophores
abstract: The absorption spectrum of aqueous indole contains contributions from the two lowest-lying excited states, La and lower-energy Lb. The corresponding fluorescence spectrum exhibits a large Stokes shift attributed to solvent-induced inversion of the excited-state ordering followed by emission from the La state. However, modeling excited-state relaxation mechanisms in aqueous indole is challenging because the two excited states are strongly coupled in a condensed-phase environment.

title: A Solid-Phase Platform for Site-Specific Thiolation and Thioether Functionalization of DNA Oligonucleotides
abstract: Thionucleobases provide distinctive hydrogen-bonding, electronic, and photochemical properties, but their site-specific incorporation into DNA often requires specialized sulfurcontaining phosphoramidites and multistep monomer synthesis. Here, we establish a unified protocol using sodium hydrosulfide (NaSH) and 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU) for direct on-support conversion of 8-bromo-2′-deoxyadenosine (Br 8 dA) to 8-thio-2′deoxyadenosine (s 8 dA), late-stage C8 thioether diversification, and concurrent conversion of Br 8 dA and 4-triazolylthymidine within a single DNA strand.

title: A General Approach to Highly Substituted 1,2-Azaborines via Borylative Benzannulation of Unsaturated Imines
abstract: Highly substituted, monocyclic 1,2-azaborines could expand the chemical space available for benzene bioisosterism; however, their synthesis remains an unmet challenge. Here we report a general, modular, transition-metal-free strategy that couples unsaturated imines with dihaloboranes to construct diverse 1,2-azaborines through a borylative benzannulation pathway. This method provides efficient access to tetra-, penta-, and hexa-substituted azaborines, including fused, macrocyclic and heteroatom-substituted scaffolds.

title: Facet-Dependent Redox Reversibility Governs the Stability of IrO2 Surfaces under Dynamic Electrochemical Potentials
abstract: Understanding catalyst stability under fluctuating potentials is essential for renewable-powered water electrolysis, yet the surface processes governing degradation remain unclear. Here, we investigate IrO2(110) and IrO2(100) single-crystal thin films under potential cycling relevant to renewable-powered proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis. The activity of IrO2(110) increased after cycling, whereas IrO2(100) deactivated. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated higher Ir valence on both facets, accompanied by a pronounced increase in surface OH species only on (110).

title: BiFuN: Machine Learning-Guided Bifunctional Catalysis in Hydrogenation Reactions
abstract: Hydrogen activation and further hydrogenation of substrate cover chemical processes in synthetic and energetic-related technologies. In homogeneous catalysis, transition metal complexes with bifunctional nature offer a platform for the activation and later utilization of the hydrogen-source. However, the development of new catalysts is limited by long-term trial-and-error practices. Screening approaches offer the possibility of relying on key properties to identify promising candidates.

title: PolyGLOT: Graph-Token Language Modeling for Unified Polymer Property Prediction and Programmable Generation
abstract: Polymer design benefits from representations that combine efficient sequence modeling with explicit access to molecular graph structure. String representations provide compact sequences but most remain sensitive to syntax and connectivity errors, whereas sequential graph generation becomes more costly as molecular graphs grow. We introduce PolyGLOT (Polymer Graph Language of Tokens), which represents a linear homopolymer repeat unit as a reconstructable sequence of mostly small molecular subgraphs.

title: TLQ Method: A Tandem Mixing–Linear Deduction–Quantile Weighted Median Framework for Robust Metabolite Screening and a General Diagnostic Indicator for Measurement Reliability
abstract: Untargeted metabolomics is constrained by inter-individual variability, difficulty in detecting low-abundance metabolites, and matrix effects. Post-acquisition corrections are limited when biological variation is large, signals approach detection limits, or matrix effects are strong. We propose the TLQ method, consisting of Tandem Mixing, Linear Deduction, and Quantile Quality-Weighted Median. Tandem Mixing compresses between-group matrix differences and enhances low-abundance signals via equal-volume mixing of paired samples.

title: Denitrative Cyanation of Nitroalkanes by Nucleophilic Substitution through Anion–Radical Coupling
abstract: We report a photocatalytic denitrative cyanation to directly convert nitroalkanes into nitriles under mild conditions. The reaction proceeds rapidly under blue LED irradiation and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic investigations support an anion–radical coupling pathway between an α-nitro radical and a cyanide ion. In this mechanism, a nitronate ion undergoes single-electron oxidation to generate an α-nitro radical, which is intercepted by a cyanide ion to form an α-nitronitrile radical anion.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Machine learning forecasting of teak (Tectona grandis L.f.) growth parameters in Ghanaian plantations: a plot-level grouped-split analysis with ablation and sensitivity analysis
abstract: Ghana lacks a centralized, publicly archived permanent sample plot inventory for teak (Tectona grandis L.f.) plantations, which limits growth and yield models that use current field data. This constraint motivates model-extracted training data built from published allometric and site relationships, paired with machine learning, as a route to forecasting tools that can be updated once field inventory becomes available. This study built and tested a multilayer perceptron (GrowthMLP) that forecasts total height and stem volume of Ghana teak from stand, soil, and topographic covariates. Tree-level records (n = 4,995) were extracted using Ghana-calibrated allometric and yield relationships and merged with soil and topographic covariates from two published chronosequence studies. Several tree records were extracted for the same published plot and therefore share identical or near-identical stand and site covariates. To account for this, all data were split at plot level rather than at row level: every tree from a given plot was assigned to exactly one of training, validation, or test, guaranteeing zero shared plots across partitions. A 21-configuration ablation grid tested feature groups, network depth, dropout rate, normalization, and target set on this plot-level 70/15/15 split, training each configuration for up to 120 epochs. The selected model retained all 26 available predictors, used a three-hidden-layer network (512, 256, 128) with a dropout rate of 0.1, and reached a mean test R² of 0.903 and a mean test root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.294 across height and volume. Stem volume reached a test R² of 0.991, while total height reached 0.816. Diameter at breast height, dominant height, and stand age ranked as the most influential individual predictors under permutation importance. Soil chemical properties as a group produced the largest swing in height error under coordinated perturbation, consistent with field evidence that soil fertility shapes teak growth. Removing the two soil feature groups reduced mean test R² to 0.898, a small but real cost once plot-level leakage was eliminated. A moderate multilayer perceptron can reproduce Ghana teak growth relationships from stand, soil, and site data with high fidelity for volume and reasonable fidelity for height, when evaluated on plots entirely unseen during training. Field permanent sample plot data remain the definitive next step for testing these forecasts outside the allometric relationships used to build them.

title: Table-Based Text Parsing Methods for Polymer Science: A Comparative Study
abstract: Polymer informatics has emerged as an area of interest in the search for more sustainable plastics. Yet, there is a dearth in large, high-quality, polymer-based materials databases that are open-source for the polymer research community. Efforts to curate such databases involve autogenerating large experimental materials databases by mining chemical data from scientific literature, with a specific focus on mining tabular data as these are particularly rich sources of polymeric information. This study compares the performance of two tools in extracting large volumes of tabular data about polymer names and their glass-transition, melting and decomposition temperatures: a table-extraction tool that employs a downstream neural network to resolve polymer names from the table fields, and the table-mining part of the "chemistry-aware" natural-language-processing tool, ChemDataExtractor. We find that both methods afford high precision. The recall of the former is boosted by preserving some of the implicit structure of the source tables, while the latter offers a far wider scope of knowledge extraction from the literature on polymer science.

title: Oxidative C–C Bond Cleavage of 1,2-Diols by Mn-Doped CeO2 Catalysts
abstract: The 1,2-diol motif is frequently found in biomass-derived compounds; thus, its direct and selective C–C bond cleavage is crucial for broadening the utility of biomass resources. In this paper, we report that CeO2 showed high catalytic activity for the C–C bond cleavage of 1,2-diols. Moreover, Mn-doped CeO2 demonstrated higher activity than pristine CeO2, enabling the efficient conversion of 1,2-diols into the corresponding carbonyl compounds in high yields.

title: Modeling Reaction Feasibility to Identify New Opportunities for Sigmatropic Rearrangements
abstract: Defining the scope and limitations of synthetic methods enables bolder, lower-risk synthetic design. Computation can facilitate this if able to anticipate reaction success or failure. Herein, we combine a machine-learned interatomic potential with the TS-tools package for high-throughput prediction of transition state geometries and barriers for hypothetical reactions. We focus on sigmatropic rearrangements, which are of synthetic interest, enable non-obvious retrosynthetic disconnections, and are explicable by electronic structure theory.

title: In situ light-coupled TEM separates photochemical and radiolytic degradation in halide perovskites
abstract: Metal halide perovskites degrade under the same illumination that powers them, yet nanoscale observation of this photochemistry is confounded by electron-beam damage in transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We introduce an optical-fiber-coupled closed-cell TEM platform with independent control over electron dose rate, illumination wavelength and power density, and gas environment, and use it to decouple photochemical from radiolytic degradation in CsPbBr3 in real time.

title: Site-Specific Speciation of Vanadium Sites on γ-Al2O3 Facets and Edges from 51V SSNMR Spectroscopy
abstract: γ-alumina (γ-Al2O3) supported vanadium oxide represent a notable class of heterogenous catalysts used for the direct oxidative propane dehydrogenation (ODH) reaction. However, while the presence of highly dispersed VOx (V5+) species has been established, understanding the exact structure of surface sites and the role of supports remains a pivotal objective for establishing structure-property relationships.

title: ELECTROSTATIC MODEL OF COVALENT BONDING. A PARTICULAR SOLUTION OF THE HELLMANN – FEYNMAN ELECTROSTATIC THEOREM
abstract: The purpose of this work was to create a model of a covalent bond based on quasi-classical electrostatic concepts. A three-center electrostatic model of a covalent bond has been proposed, which takes into account only the forces that occur along the axis connecting the nuclei of the bonded atoms. These electrostatic forces are represented as gradients of the potential energy of the atoms from their isolated state to their bonded state.

title: Bioadhesive Linear-Dendritic Block Copolymer Hydrogels for Wound Closure and Localized Antibiotic Delivery
abstract: Surgical adhesives have emerged as a less invasive alternative than classical sutures, yet many suffer from poor adhesion, poor compatibility with skin, and lack of antibacterial properties. To address these limitations, we developed a new class of dual-functional hydrogels combining strong tissue adhesion with localized antimicrobial activity. These hydrogels were formulated by blending catechol-functionalized linear-dendritic block copolymers (LDBC(cat)8) with UV-crosslinkable acrylate-terminated analogues (LDBC(acr)4), resulting in soft and interpenetrated hybrid network that combines…

title: Spatially Differentiated Multi-Sectoral Mitigation Strategies Needed to Reduce PM2.5 Exposures in India
abstract: Air pollution in India contributes to approximately 1 million deaths annually due to exposure to ambient fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ). Here, we demonstrate that interventions to achieve the goals of India’s National Clean Air Program require adopting a multi-sector, multi-scale approach to link air pollution sources to human exposure. To support this objective, we developed PAVITRA (Air pollution management and intervention tool for India), a computationally efficient and high-fidelity air quality management tool.

title: Deep Eutectic Solvents as novel food ingredients: biosafety assessment of water-based DESs (aquoDESs) extracts from spent coffee grounds
abstract: The recovery of bioactive compounds, such as caffeine and chlorogenic acids, from spent coffee grounds (SCGs) represents a promising opportunity for developing functional food ingredients. However, the direct incorporation of extracts into food matrices requires rigorous safety validation of both the extraction solvent and the resulting extract. In this study, two food-grade water-based deep eutectic solvents (aquoDESs), trimethylglycine:water (TMG:H2O) and glycerol:water (Glyc:H2O) and their corresponding SCGs extracts at different dilutions (1:1, 1:5, 1:10) were evaluated in terms of…

title: Utilizing Electrosorption for Efficient Removal of Polyethylene Microplastics from Water: Critical Factors and Mechanistic Insights
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) produced by human activities can enter the environment through wastewater systems. A significant quantity of MPs still reaches the environment via wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluent because the techniques commonly used in WWTPs are not effective at removing MPs, especially smaller particles. To address this, an electrosorption (ES) method was developed in this study to separate MPs (3–5 µm polyethylene particles) from water using graphite felt electrodes.

title: Solvent-Dependent Self-Association of Chiral 2-Acetoxy-2-Phenylacetic Acid Revealed by Infrared and Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectroscopy
abstract: The solvent-dependent self-association of chiral 2-acetoxy-2-phenylacetic acid (APA) was investigated in CCl4, CDCl3, and DMSO-d6 solvents, using infrared (IR) and Vibrational Circular Dichroism (VCD) spectroscopy, supported by density functional theory calculations. Concentration-dependent IR measurements revealed progressive formation of self-associated species in CCl4 and CDCl3, whereas no significant concentration dependence was observed in DMSO-d6.

title: Role of ortho-functional groups in stabilizing catechol surface complexes on ferrite nanoparticles
abstract: Molecular-level interactions of naturally occurring catechol derivatives with ferrite surfaces were investigated using permanently magnetic barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets and superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles. Catechol (1,2-benzenediol) and guaiacol (2-methoxyphenol) were selected as representative aromatic ligands relevant to catechol- and guaiacyl-containing natural compounds.

title: Computational Screening of Functional Nanocluster Precursors for Bottle-around-Ship Encapsulation in Metal-Organic Frameworks
abstract: Monodisperse, Atomically Precise Nanoclusters (APNCs) exhibit distinct electronic and sizedependent properties, making them uniquely suited for catalysis, sensing, and drug delivery applications. However, their controlled synthesis remains a challenge since the existing methods struggle to reproducibly achieve atomic-level precision in their composition and geometry.

title: Engineering transparent-electrode surface chemistry for robust molecular interfaces in perovskite photovoltaics
abstract: The chemical state of transparent oxide electrodes critically determines the formation and durability of selfassembled monolayer (SAM) contacts in perovskite photovoltaics. Although standard cleaning 1 (SC1) and ultraviolet–ozone (UVO) treatments are individually established approaches for oxide-surface modification, their complementary functions in regulating molecular interfaces remain poorly understood.

title: Temperature-and potential-induced exfoliation of electrochemically produced solid carbon from CO2 on a Ce:GaInSn electrode
abstract: Resource-efficient carbon dioxide removal from the atmosphere will require the development of new materials for processes beyond carbon capture and utilisation. One high-potential pathway for such negative emission technologies is the electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to storable products such as graphitic carbon. Although this can be achieved by employing an electrode made of cerium particles in a liquid gallium-indium-tin matrix, this electrocatalytic pathway currently suffers from comparatively low faradaic efficiencies (FE).

title: Nanocorrugation-Reorganized PEDOT:PSS Electrochemical Transistors for Ultrasensitive Biomolecular Detection
abstract: Although electrolyte-gated organic transistor (EGOT) biosensors enable label-free volumetric biosensing, their sensitivity in physiological environments remains fundamentally limited by poor polymer microstructure ordering and inefficient ion–channel coupling. This paper introduces EGOTs with geometrically reconfigured mixed ionic–electronic transport enabled by nanocorrugated poly(3,4ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) channels.

title: OptoMatKG: A Traceable Knowledge Graph Framework with Semantic Retrieval for Optoelectronic Materials Science
abstract: Extracting and correlating knowledge from heterogeneous scientific publications poses a fundamental data engineering challenge for data-driven materials discovery. Traditional keyword search lacks semantic depth, while generic large language models (LLMs) are prone to hallucinated predictions. To address these limitations, we present OptoMatKG, a literature-scale data engineering system whose core contributions are threefold: (1) a domain-specific knowledge graph construction pipeline based on a nine-category fullworkflow ontology; the resulting graph comprises 2.62 million entities and 3.38…

title: Atmospheric CO2 splitting using a visible light-driven Z-scheme photocatalyst in a gas-phase flow reactor
abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) coupled to photocatalytic CO 2 splitting offers a route to simultaneously mitigate atmospheric CO 2 accumulation and produce sustainable fuels. However, integrations of DAC with photocatalytic CO 2 conversion have thus far relied on ultraviolet-light-absorbing TiO 2 and organic substrate oxidation, limiting solar energy utilisation and precluding a truly artificial photosynthetic reaction.

title: Breakdown and Classification of Adiabatic-Connection Convexity in Coulomb Systems
abstract: Convexity of the density-fixed adiabatic-connection integrand is widely observed but is not fixed by the variational structure of density-functional theory. We show that it is not universal for ordinary three-dimensional electrons with the bare Coulomb interaction. Equal-step third differences of the Levy functional give a derivative-free classification into convex, affine, concave, and mixed classes, while an exact response identity determines the local sign at regular fixed-density points.

title: GLOSS: A Multi-Strategy Sampling Algorithm for Optimization in Vast Chemical Spaces
abstract: Surrogate-based optimization accelerates closed-loop scientific discovery. In chemistry and materials science, however, sparse data over vast chemical spaces make surrogate predictions unreliable and undermine data efficiency. We develop GLOSS, a sampling algorithm that divides each batch across three complementary strategies: Global, Local, and Unexplored. Across multiple benchmarks, GLOSS reaches 95% of the optimum about twice as fast as Bayesian optimization and consistently outperforms genetic algorithms and random sampling, and its advantage grows more pronounced as the chemical space…

title: Linear-response TDDFT simulations of K-edge resonant inelastic X-ray scattering in extended systems
abstract: We present an implementation for the calculation of K-edge resonant inelastic X-ray scattering spectra based on time-dependent density functional theory in the CP2K package. The method evaluates the Kramers-Heisenberg cross section from transition dipole moments connecting the ground state, core-excited intermediate states, and valence-excited final states. The present implementation combines the existing linear response time-dependent density functional theory modules (XAS-TDP and TDDFT) within a unified framework.

title: Understanding Aggregate Structures of Organic Donor-Acceptor Systems by Partitioning Repulsive Interactions into Orbital-Orbital Contributions
abstract: Molecular Orbital-Pair Contributions to the Exchange repulsion (MOPCE) are used to elucidate the orbital origin of repulsive interactions and to understand their role in determining the stacking arrangements of organic donor–acceptor (DA) complexes. We investigate three DA complexes with planar monomers, benzene–p-benzoquinone (BZ–pBQ), benzene–tetracyanoethylene (BZ–TCNE), and tetrathiafulvalene–tetracyanoquinodimethane (TTF–TCNQ), which prefer distinct stacking geometries.

title: Pressing Mode Determines Densification Uniformity and Dimensional Stability in Sulfide Solid-State Batteries
abstract: Pressure-assisted densification is essential for manufacturing sulfide solid-state batteries because electrochemical performance critically depends on intimate solid–solid contact within the electrode stack. However, how the applied stress state governs the co-densification of mechanically dissimilar layers and their electrochemical functionality remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the pressure-assisted consolidation of Li6PS5Cl separator/composite cathode bilayers under uniaxial and isostatic loading.

title: Polarity-resolved imaging reveals active transport in catalytic Janus nanomotors
abstract: Catalytic Janus motors that convert chemical energy into self-propulsion are promising platforms for targeted delivery, sensing, and environmental remediation. Miniaturizing these systems to the nanoscale is challenged by rotational diffusion (𝑫r ∝ 1/𝑹3) increasing faster than translational diffusion (𝑫t ∝ 1/𝑹), which destroys orientational memory. This raises the question of whether catalytic asymmetry can still bias the active displacement direction when orientational memory is short-lived.

title: Learning Multiscale Computational Strategies for Supramolecular Recognition
abstract: Accurate prediction of host-guest binding affinities with end-point free energy approaches requires a balance between molecular sampling, energetic description, and computational cost, yet the relative importance and interplay of these factors remain poorly understood for chemically diverse supramolecular systems. Here, we establish a systematic benchmark of end-point affinity calculations across more than 300 host-guest pairs involving pillararenes, cucurbiturils, octa acid, and cyclodextrins.

title: From Proteins and Molecules to Cats and Dogs: Visualization as Scalable Minimum Spanning Trees
abstract: Dimensionality reduction and data visualization are essential for analyzing highdimensional datasets, yet traditional projection methods obscure local structural relationships. We present TMAP2, a scalable rewrite of TMAP that maps highdimensional data as a minimum spanning tree. TMAP2 accepts diverse input types, including continuous embeddings, sparse fingerprints, and precomputed graphs, and applies to single-cell, image, chemistry, or protein-language-model data. Every line on the map is therefore a real nearest-neighbor relationship, and exactly one path joins any two points.

title: Molecular Hydrogen Governs Zinc-Based Battery Failure
abstract: Zinc is among the most promising anode materials for sustainable aqueous batteries, yet its practical deployment is limited by poor interfacial stability and insufficient durability. Because the thermodynamic stability of zinc is incompatible with the water stability window, corrosion and hydrogen evolution inevitably accompany zinc electrochemistry in aqueous electrolytes. Despite being an inherent product of zinc corrosion, molecular hydrogen (H2) has largely been regarded as a passive by-product rather than an active contributor to zinc degradation and dendrite formation.

title: Computational shielding of dengue viral prefusion with permeable cyclic-minipeptides
abstract: Permeable cyclic-minipeptide-conformer candidates have been computationally cogenerated to shield the protected prefusionloops (FL) of dengue flavivirus (DENV). The objective was to prevent the pH-dependent dissociation events that trigger flavivirus fusion/ infectivity by exposing the FL highlyconserved sequences to homotrimer fusioncompetent conformations. For that, hundreds of BoltzGen candidates were co-generated targeting a prefusion minimized DENV envelope AB heterodimer (minEAB) model including both EA-protective and EB-FL sequences.

title: Contrast-Engineered Polymeric Nanoparticles Enable Multicomponent SAXS Imaging in Soft Matter
abstract: Selective visualization of multiple organic components in small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) studies remains a major challenge in complex soft matter systems due to limited electron density contrast. Here, we introduce contrast-engineered polymeric nanoparticles (PNPs) as organic probes for multicomponent SAXS imaging. Well-defined, monomodal cationic PNPs prepared by polymerization-induced self-assembly (PISA) were loaded with the iodine-containing molecule 1,4-diiodobenzene, increasing particle electron density while preserving particle size, morphology, colloidal stability, and surface…

title: Heteroatom-doped fullerene C60 nanoclusters as tunable carriers for a thiazole-sulfonohydrazide lead compound: A DFT study of B, Al, Si, Ga and Ge substitution
abstract: Selective recognition of pharmacologically relevant heteroaromatic lead compounds is important for developing molecular sensing and responsive nanocarrier platforms. C60 fullerene is an attractive nanocluster scaffold because of its stable curved π-conjugated cage and rich electronic structure, but its weakly polarized surface often requires chemical tuning to improve specific host-guest interactions. C60 fullerene and its heteroatom-doped derivatives were investigated as tunable nanocluster platforms for molecular adsorption and electronic sensing using DFT and TD-DFT calculations.

title: Identification of Xanthine Oxidase Inhibiting Fractions Containing Low-Molecular-Weight Melanoidins Obtained from Lightly Roasted Barley Products
abstract: Lightly roasted barley flour exhibits xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibitory activity despite containing negligible amounts of pyrogallol, which has been identified as a potent XO inhibitor in highly roasted barley tea. This study aimed to identify the XO-inhibitory compounds responsible for this activity. Assay-guided fractionation of lightly roasted barley extract using octadecyl silica gel (ODS) revealed that the active fractions were not attributable to pyrogallol.

title: A Multi-Coordinate Carbide Ligand as the Anchor for Reactive Transition Metal Clusters: Oxidative Addition, Adduct Formation and Catalytic Hydrosilylation with a Pentanuclear Nickel Carbide Cluster
abstract: The reactivity of a pentanuclear carbide cluster, [( i Pr 3 P)Ni] 5 (µ 5 -C)H 4 ( 1 ), with a variety of reagents was examined. The addition of 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)aniline to 1 resulted in reversible N­­—H bond oxidative addition, forming [( i Pr 3 P)NiH] 5 (µ 4 -C)[N(H)C 6 H 3 ( m -CF 3 ) 2 ] ( 2 ), with a [Ni 5 ] 10+ core. Exposing 1 to neopentyl chloride produced the paramagnetic nickel carbide cluster [( i Pr 3 P)Ni] 5 (µ 5 -C)H 4 (µ 2 -Cl) ( 3 ) from a one-electron oxidation, as well as the homodimerized product 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane.

title: Stannylene hydrides as key intermediates in redox neutral Sn(II)/Sn(II) catalysis: Hydrodefluorination as a case study
abstract: Low-valent tin hydrides display hydride donor properties that differ markedly from those of conventional organotin(IV) hydrides, yet their catalytic applications have remained largely confined to reactions of polar multiple bonds. Herein, we exploit this distinct reactivity for catalytic C–F bond activation and investigate the mechanism underlying the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes. An isolable diketiminate-supported Sn(II) fluoride efficiently catalyses the reaction using phenylsilane as terminal hydride source.

title: Same Substitutions, Opposite Residence Times: Target-Dependent Kinetic Inversion of Diazabicyclooctane 𝛽-Lactamase Inhibitors
abstract: Reversible covalent inhibitors are governed by both formation and breakdown of the covalent complex, yet matched medicinal-chemistry modifications are often interpreted through affinity or potency alone. We performed an original quantitative reanalysis of published experimental kinetics and corresponding covalent crystal structures for four diazabicyclooctane (DBO) inhibitors—avibactam, FPI-1465, FPI-1523, and FPI-1602—against CTX-M-15 and OXA-48.

title: Product-Specific Isotope Effects as Constraints on Branched Catalytic Reaction Networks
abstract: Rates and selectivities alone often cannot distinguish between competing mechanisms in branched catalytic reactions. Here, we use GC–IRMS at natural carbon-isotope abundance to measure the isotope compositions of both CO and CH4 formed during CO2 hydrogenation over SiO2-supported Ni and Co nanoparticles. Comparing the isotope effects of both products, rather than considering either product alone, allows us to test whether their pathways share intermediates and where the isotope-sensitive steps occur.

title: First-principles Investigation of Reconstructions for the Polar CoO (111) Surface and the Impact on Nanoparticle Morphology
abstract: Reconstructions of the polar CoO (111) surface defines critical properties that impacts application in catalysis, energy storage and electrochemistry. However, these surface reconstructions are relatively unexplored, compared to its isomorphic analogues, and greater understanding of CoO surfaces is needed to enable rational control of surface stability and reactivity. We investigate the surface reconstructions of the polar (111) facet of rocksalt CoO in equilibrium with an oxygen environment using first principles calculations in conjunction with surface thermodynamics.

title: The Mechanochemical Reset for Coordination Self-Assembly.
abstract: Self-assembly is a canonical process for generating ordered, functional architectures, with the structural 'blueprint' encoded in the component design and interaction thermodynamics. While external stimuli such as concentration and chemical guests might shift the equilibrium between predefined ordered states, the structural memory remains embedded in the assembly (thermodynamic control). In this work, we employ mechanical force as a unique stimulus to dismantle thermodynamic order, accessing a structural “erasing” state and resetting the assembly landscape.

title: Photochemical Carbamate Scission Redefines Metal-Based PhotoCORMs through Multi-Output Activation
abstract: Metal-based photoCORMs (Photoactivatable carbon monoxide-releasing molecules) have traditionally relied on photolabile M–CO bonds, constraining modular design and limiting opportunities for integrating additional functions. Here we report a modular metalbased platform in which CO generation is encoded within a photolabile carbamate rather than a M–CO bond, enabling visible-light-controlled, spatiotemporal CO release while preserving the synthetic flexibility to integrate multimodal functions within a single molecular architecture.

title: Deep drug design for molecular scaffold hopping
abstract: Structure-based virtual screening serves as a primary approach for ligand prioritization from large molecular libraries, but accurately predicting the activity of chemical entities on novel drug targets remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present an interactome-based graph transformer network for rapid bioactivity prediction and de novo ligand design. Integrating three-dimensional pocket geometry with two-dimensional ligand graphs yields a joint representation for direct affinity prediction, which generalizes well across sparse datasets.

title: LCMD[db]: The Unified Chemical Data Hosting and Analysis Platform
abstract: Chemical datasets used in computational chemistry are often distributed across separate repositories, stored in dataset-specific formats, and accompanied by heterogeneous metadata, property definitions, and structure representations. This fragmentation increases the manual preprocessing required to reuse datasets for molecular property prediction, reaction modeling, benchmarking, and machine-learning workflows. Here, we present LCMD-db, a chemical data hosting and analysis platform for organizing molecular, fragment, and reaction datasets within a common framework.

title: Dynamic Evolution and Stability of Ketenes in MAPO-18 (M = Si or Mg): Molecular Insights into the Reaction Mechanism for CO2-to-Hydrocarbons
abstract: AEI topology molecular sieves (MAPO-18) have shown promising properties as components of OX-ZEO type tandem catalysts, where the Brønsted acid sites (BAS) introduced by different framework substitutions lead to distinct catalytic mechanisms on the CO2-to-hydrocarbons conversion. Ketenes are key intermediates in the conversion of methanol to hydrocarbons. This study provides molecular-level insights into the reactions of three ketenes (ketene, methyl ketene, and dimethyl ketene) with the BAS in MAPO-18 (M = Si, Mg) molecular sieves at operando conditions through first-principles molecular…

title: Antimicrobial and cytotoxic activity of 2-amino-4H-chromenes
abstract: Although some 2-amino-4H-chromenes displayed moderate activity against S. mitis (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, and 10), S. salivarius (3 and 9), and L. paracasei (1 and 6), most of the compounds displayed weak activity against most of the bacteria involved in dental caries and were inactive against C. albicans and C. krusei. On the other hand, compounds 4 (IC50 < 2.47 µM, SI > 2564) and 8 (IC50 = 37.74 µM, SI > 154.80) displayed the highest anticancer activity against the MCF-7 and HeLa cell lines.

title: Energy Transfer (EnT) Catalysed [4+2] Cycloaddition of Non-Symmetrical Dienes: From Mechanistic Anomaly to Fully Functional Reaction Pathway
abstract: Harnessing the reactivity of triplet biradicals to selectively access unconventional cycloaddition pathways remains a fundamental challenge in energy transfer (EnT) catalysis. Herein, we demonstrate that systematic variation of diene substitution can redirect the intrinsic [2+2] reactivity of non-symmetrical dienes towards highly selective [4+2] cycloaddition. Notably, incorporation of a traceless vicinal BPin group invokes a non-conventional [4+2] pathway providing polysubstituted cyclohexenes with excellent regio- and diastereoselectivity.

title: Electroanalytical approaches for understanding the influence of applied potential on sensor biofouling
abstract: Biofouling is a complex and dynamic process that remains a major limitation to continuous and longterm sensing in biological environments. Unlike passive biomaterials, electrochemical sensors operate under electrical control, yet the influence of applied potential on protein adsorption and the resulting electroanalytical response is insufficiently understood. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) with redox probes of different interfacial sensitivities was used to assess the influence of positive, open-circuit, and negative polarization during bovine serum albumin (BSA) incubation on the electrochemical…

title: Operating conditions redefine the governing principles of catalyst-layer fabrication
abstract: Optimal catalyst-layer fabrication strategies for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) are often developed under a single set of operating conditions, making it unclear whether the resulting design rules remain valid across different operating environments. Here, we show that operating conditions not only shift catalyst-layer optima but re-order the fabrication parameters governing performance.

title: Ancillary Ligand Engineering Controls Supramolecular Host Architecture
abstract: Ancillary ligands (ALs) in coordination cages are commonly regarded as passive protecting groups whose primary role is to stabilize discrete cages and prevent formation of extended coordination networks. Here, we introduce ancillary ligand engineering (ALE) as a strategy for controlling the topology and dynamics of palladium-based coordination cages without modifying the metal or triimidazoylbenzene panel ligand.

title: Novel ebselen-based building block for the solid phase synthesis of selenopeptides
abstract: Although some organic selenocompounds exhibit significant therapeutic potential, synthetic access to selenopeptides remains severely limited due to complex postassembly functionalizations strategies. To overcome these limitations, we developed a stable, ebselen-derived lysine compatible with standard Fmoc/tBu solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). We synthesized the Fmoc-Lys(Ebs)-OH building block in five steps, characterizing it by HRMS and NMR spectroscopy.

title: Rational Design of a Red-Light Absorbing dinuclear Ruthenium (II) Complex with Photodynamic potential
abstract: Conventional chemotherapeutic agents often suffer from systemic toxicity, poor selectivity, and the emergence of drug resistance, highlighting the urgent need for alternative anticancer strategies. In this context, light-activated therapies have emerged as promising minimally invasive approaches for controlled cancer treatment. However, the development of single molecular systems capable of integrating multiple photoinduced therapeutic mechanisms remains challenging.

title: Open Sesame! Simulation of the Adsorption Induced Phase Transformation Mechanism of MOF Nanocrystallites
abstract: One of the most compelling features of certain MOFs is their ability to undergo stimuli-induced phase transformations with large changes in the accessible pore volume, leading to phenomena like “gate opening”. Theoretical simulations are an indispensable tool in order to understand such processes on a molecular level. However, adsorption phenomena are usually investigated within the approximation of periodic boundary conditions (PBC) and using Grand Canonical methods.

title: Identifiability Boundaries in Dynamic GPCR Pharmacology: When Desensitization, Internalization and Persistent Signaling Become Mechanistically Indistinguishable
abstract: Dynamic GPCR pharmacology increasingly relies on time-resolved signaling to infer receptor regulation, trafficking, and ligand residence, yet a kinetic response need not uniquely identify the mechanism that produced it. We developed minimal quantitative receptor-pharmacology models to determine when desensitization, internalization, persistent intracellular signaling, and slow receptor occupancy are distinguishable from a common downstream signal. We first derived exact input–output equivalences.

title: Oxygen-Necessitated Dissociation of Photoinduced Ground-State Charge-Transfer Complexes for Open-Air Synthesis of Block and Graft Copolymers
abstract: Molecular oxygen is universally regarded as an inhibitor of radical photopolymerization, necessitating rigorous deoxygenation and introducing obligatory induction periods. Here we report that a persistent photoinduced ground-state charge-transfer complex (PCTC), formed between a naphthalimide acceptor and a tertiary-amine donor, undergoes selective dissociation upon exposure to molecular oxygen.

title: A dynamic active-site water molecule drives the photocatalysis in fatty acid photodecarboxylase
abstract: Fatty acid photodecarboxylase (FAP) is a flavin-based photoenzyme that uses blue light to convert fatty acids into hydrocarbons, an attractive platform for sustainable fuel production. Its efficiency is set by a competition between photoinduced electron transfer, productive decarboxylation and unproductive back electron transfer, yet how the protein controls this competition at the atomistic level remains unresolved.

title: 4D-STEM Strain Mapping of Polycrystalline Core-shell Nanoparticles
abstract: Metal nanoparticles play a key role in sustainable chemical conversions, energy storage and electronics. Lattice strain strongly influences the functional properties of these nanoparticles and enables precise tuning of their properties. Strain can vary substantially within single nanoparticles that exhibit defect sites and grain boundaries. However, experimentally evaluating local strain distributions within such polycrystalline nanoparticles is challenging and requires the development of new characterization methods.

title: Clinical feasibility and image quality assessment of deep learning-based virtual contrast enhancement from photon-counting computed tomography
abstract: ObjectivesThe purpose of this study was to evaluate image quality and diagnostic performance of deep learning-based virtual contrast-enhanced (VCE) images generated from photon-counting CT (PCCT) datasets.Material and methodsForty consecutive patients who underwent contrast-enhanced PCCT were retrospectively included and divided into training (n = 20) and testing (n = 20) cohorts. A supervised U-Net-based convolutional neural network was trained to generate VCE images from virtual non-contrast inputs, using true contrast-enhanced (TC) images as the reference. Quantitative similarity was assessed using the structural similarity index measure (SSIM), mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Qualitative evaluation was performed independently by two radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale across thoracic and abdominal structures, with assessment of exact, ±1-point, and diagnostic agreement.ResultsQuantitative analysis demonstrated high similarity between VCE and TC images, with very high SSIM and PSNR values and low MAE, while MSE showed a right-skewed distribution. Qualitatively, VCE images were consistently rated lower than TC images. However, central thoracic vascular structures, cardiac chambers, and mediastinal lymph nodes were frequently rated as diagnostic (Likert ≥3) with high diagnostic agreement. In contrast, abdominal solid organs and vessels were often judged non-diagnostic, mainly due to heterogeneous enhancement and apparent contrast defects.ConclusionThe synthesis of VCE images from PCCT datasets is feasible and shows excellent quantitative similarity to TC images, with promising results for thoracic applications but limited reliability for abdominal evaluation at this stage.

title: Neurodevelopmental reward dysregulation and addiction risk in ADHD
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with an elevated risk of substance use disorders (SUDs), yet most affected individuals do not develop addiction, indicating that vulnerability is selectively distributed rather than intrinsic to the disorder itself. This Review synthesizes current evidence on the neurodevelopmental mechanisms linking ADHD to SUD vulnerability, examines reward-related dysregulation as a unifying mechanistic framework underlying this association, and proposes a subgroup-based precision psychiatry perspective to explain the heterogeneity of addiction risk among individuals with ADHD. Integrating evidence across genetics, molecular neuroscience, neurodevelopment, systems-level circuitry, computational modeling, and environmental modulation, converging findings implicate polygenic variation affecting synaptic and dopaminergic pathways that interacts with atypical maturation of frontostriatal and frontocortical systems supporting reward valuation, inhibitory control, and salience processing. These multilayered perturbations may manifest computationally as dysregulated reinforcement learning, including altered dopamine signaling dynamics and impaired integration of delayed outcomes, biasing decision-making toward immediate reward. At the circuit level, disrupted coordination between mesolimbic reward systems and prefrontal control networks may facilitate a shift from goal-directed behavior to habit-based responding following repeated substance exposure, further shaped by experience-dependent neuroplasticity. Importantly, available evidence suggests that addiction risk is concentrated within distinct ADHD subgroups characterized by reduced responsiveness to anticipated rewards, impaired reinforcement learning, preference for immediate over delayed rewards, impaired inhibitory control, emotional dysregulation, and impulsive decision-making that emerge and evolve across development. Collectively, this synthesis supports a precision psychiatry framework integrating genetic, neuroimaging, computational, and digital phenotyping approaches to improve the identification, prediction, and prevention of SUD vulnerability in ADHD.
venue: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience

title: Deviation from Fermi-liquid $T^2$ resistivity caused by collective transport
abstract: `Fermi-liquid behavior' is nowadays used as a shorthand for quadratic temperature dependence of the electrical resistivity. In a metal, for this to occur, electrons must be cooled well below the Fermi degeneracy temperature, $T_{\mathrm{F}}$. A departure from this behavior is observed at finite temperature. Here, we note that this departure has opposite signs in two distinct types of Fermi liquids. In weakly correlated ones, the upward departure implies a higher exponent of the inelastic resistivity, attributable to \textit{additional scattering} by phonons. In contrast, there is a downward deviation in strongly correlated metals, which implies either \textit{reduced scattering} or \textit{additional conduction}, as in the case of normal liquid $^3$He, in which a distinct contribution to heat transport by a sound mode has been recently identified. Such a channel of conduction smoothly transforms across $T_{\mathrm{F}}$ to the one captured by the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of classical liquids. In three metals (UPt$_3$, Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, and heavily overdoped LSCO), according to the available experimental data, the normalized amplitude of excess conductivity at $T/T_{\mathrm{F}}\simeq0.02$ is comparable to what has been seen in $^3$He, suggesting, without establishing, a common origin.

title: Synthesis and Application of 3,3-Difluoro Sialic Acid as a Sialyltransferase and Neuraminidase Inhibitor
abstract: Sialic acid (Neu5Ac) is a monosaccharide terminating glycoconjugates, serving as ligands for lectins in health and disease. Tools to target sialyltransferases (STs) and neuraminidases (NEUs) are important in the study of sialoglycans. 3FaxNeu5Ac is a common ST inhibitor, while 2,3diFNeu5Ac is a covalent mechanism-based NEU inactivator. Here, we demonstrate the advantages of having two fluorines at C3 for both classes of inhibitors. Motivated by the finding that 3FaxNeu5Ac is transferred by STs slowly, we aimed to synthesize 3,3-difluoro-Neu5Ac (3,3diFNeu5Ac).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Local pH Control Promotes Oxygen-Atom Transfer Electrosynthesis
abstract: Control of the local reaction environment at electrified interfaces is central to electrocatalysis, yet this principle has rarely been integrated into electro-organic synthesis. Electro-organic transformations are not governed by electron transfer alone; reaction turnover is often coupled to ion transfer and, in particular, proton transfer across aqueous, mixed, and nonaqueous media. Under high-rate operation, these fluxes polarize proton activity near electrodes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
